wardley.comment: Read the lowercase header, allowing an attached statement. wardley.md#detection: The grammar accepts only the lowercase header. wardley.md#detection: The header needs no EOL: a following statement can be glued directly to it.

patterns.comment: Read native hidden YAML. wardley.md#native-padding-hidden-forms-and-eol: Hidden-yaml starts with three dashes, optional ASCII space/tab and a line break. Try a body ending in a line break before the empty-body alternative; within that first alternative take as little body as allows a qualifying closer. A closer is three dashes at the beginning of a line, followed by a consumed line break or a nonconsumed common-whitespace/end boundary. It need not use the opener’s indentation. An indented closer or four closing dashes is not that closer.

Read native hidden directives. wardley.md#native-padding-hidden-forms-and-eol: Hidden-directive starts with optional ASCII space/tab and %%{, reads any characters as few as possible through a qualifying }%%, then consumes a following line break or only tests a common-whitespace/end boundary. If an early closer is glued to nonwhitespace, try a later qualifying closer. If the whole rule fails, native-comment can read the percent pair and the rest of its line, including apparent following syntax. A native comment stops before CR/LF and consumes no line break. Its mark is %%; a single percent is not a comment.

Read native percent comments. wardley.md#native-padding-hidden-forms-and-eol: A native comment stops before CR/LF and consumes no line break. wardley.md#native-padding-hidden-forms-and-eol: Its mark is %%; a single percent is not a comment.

Read metadata text and its delimiters. wardley.md#common-metadata-values: Title-line is title and an optional separator of exactly one ASCII space/tab followed by line content. Acc-title-line and acc-descr-line have their exact keyword, optional space/tab, colon and line content. Line content stops immediately before the first %% or CR/LF; quotes are ordinary text and need not close. Title-colon is not a title form. Earlier spaced-name exclusions still apply. wardley.md#common-metadata-values: Acc-descr-block has accDescr, optional common whitespace, opening brace and content through the first closing brace. The closer is required. Quotes and backslashes do not protect a closing brace. Internal line breaks, indentation, bare percent lines and native-looking YAML remain content unless a shared removal applies; native-directive-looking text can instead close the block at its first brace.

Read command keywords at a statement start, including glued names and annotation numbers. wardley.md#keyword-and-name-boundaries: All Wardley command/header keywords and strategy values use their exact lowercase spelling without a word or whitespace boundary. Thus componentA and anchor_A split at their keyword prefixes; annotations precedes annotation. A global directive glued after a complete keyword does not add a boundary requirement after its removal. A split keyword instead follows the atomic divergence below.

Read the label-offset keyword after coordinates. wardley.md#grammar: A component has at most one label offset, one source strategy and one inertia decoration, in that order. wardley.md#common-boundaries-in-authored-components: Global directives and semicolons actually selected by the shared line rule may lie between complete authored components. A coordinate pair has bracket, number, comma, number and bracket components; offset sign and integer are separate; strategy and parenthesized inertia have parenthesis, fixed word and parenthesis components. Stage names, @, boundary, slash and second name also have separate boundaries. Common metadata separates its complete word from colon, brace or title separator.

Read an inertia decoration after coordinates or strategy, or inside parentheses. wardley.md#grammar: Inertia can be bare or parenthesized. wardley.md#common-boundaries-in-authored-components: Global directives and semicolons actually selected by the shared line rule may lie between complete authored components. A coordinate pair has bracket, number, comma, number and bracket components; offset sign and integer are separate; strategy and parenthesized inertia have parenthesis, fixed word and parenthesis components. Stage names, @, boundary, slash and second name also have separate boundaries. Common metadata separates its complete word from colon, brace or title separator.

Read a source-strategy value after its parenthesis. wardley.md#keyword-and-name-boundaries: A strategy is build, buy, outsource or market, in that priority order. wardley.md#common-boundaries-in-authored-components: Global directives and semicolons actually selected by the shared line rule may lie between complete authored components. A coordinate pair has bracket, number, comma, number and bracket components; offset sign and integer are separate; strategy and parenthesized inertia have parenthesis, fixed word and parenthesis components. Stage names, @, boundary, slash and second name also have separate boundaries. Common metadata separates its complete word from colon, brace or title separator.

Read unsigned integer or decimal units; offset signs stay separate. wardley.md#numbers: A decimal is a nonempty ASCII digit run, one dot and a nonempty ASCII digit run. Leading zeros are allowed. An integer is 0, tried first, or a nonzero ASCII digit followed by as many ASCII digits as possible without ending immediately before a dot. Decimal precedes integer. Leading-zero integers consequently split and reject where one integer is required. Plus, negative decimals, exponent notation, a missing side of the dot, NaN and Infinity spellings are not numeric units. wardley.md#numbers: Coordinates of anchors, components, notes and forces, pipeline evolution values, evolve targets and stage boundaries require decimal. Annotation and annotations-box coordinates allow decimal or integer. Size dimensions, annotation numbers and offset magnitudes require integer. An offset minus is separate punctuation, so space/tab or whole hidden forms may separate it from the unsigned magnitude. A decimal offset or size dimension rejects.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.mermaid

patterns.comment: Read the separate flow opener, quoted label and arrow marker. wardley.md#strings-and-link-labels: A port is +<>, +> or +<, in that priority order. A dependency-arrow is ->. A link-arrow is -->, -.->, >, or a labeled flow consisting of +, single-quoted content and the marker <>, < or >. Flow content contains any characters except single quote, including line breaks and U+2028/U+2029, and may be empty. Backslash is ordinary there and cannot escape a quote. Its label does not use the string escape conversion. wardley.md#common-boundaries-in-authored-components: A labeled flow has +, its whole quoted label and its ending marker as authored components. Global trivia may separate those components and may lie inside label text. A dependency arrow, a whole port and the <> marker are indivisible glyphs. A fixed keyword, strategy word, integer, decimal or id-name is also indivisible. A spaced-name is a text unit and can contain shared removals. Internal atom splits reject under the two atomic divergences below.

Read a flow label without backslash escapes. wardley.md#strings-and-link-labels: Flow content contains any characters except single quote, including line breaks and U+2028/U+2029, and may be empty. wardley.md#strings-and-link-labels: Backslash is ordinary there and cannot escape a quote.

Read ports and unlabeled arrows without splitting an earlier name. wardley.md#strings-and-link-labels: A port is +<>, +> or +<, in that priority order. A dependency-arrow is ->. A link-arrow is -->, -.->, >, or a labeled flow consisting of +, single-quoted content and the marker <>, < or >. Flow content contains any characters except single quote, including line breaks and U+2028/U+2029, and may be empty. Backslash is ordinary there and cannot escape a quote. Its label does not use the string escape conversion.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.arrow.mermaid

patterns.comment: Read a semicolon-delimited link label through the physical line end. wardley.md#strings-and-link-labels: A link-label is a semicolon followed by one or more characters other than CR/LF, taking the rest of that physical line. Bare semicolon rejects; semicolon-space is a nonempty authored literal even when its derived value is empty, and two semicolons give content consisting of the second one. U+2028/U+2029 and native-looking hidden forms remain label content. Keep this label separately even when a flow label takes precedence in the Db. Derived label and flow rules belong to the tests summary, not the authored arrow fields. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.

Read a quoted name or text. wardley.md#strings-and-link-labels: A string uses matching single or double quotes, may be empty and must close. Read nonmatching-quote, nonbackslash characters or a backslash with exactly one following character until the unescaped matching quote. The character after a backslash cannot be a normalized LF, U+2028 or U+2029. Unescaped physical line breaks and both separators are content. A missing closer or dangling backslash rejects. Common quote conversion applies before this matching; authored quotes and escape spelling remain in StringLiteral.raw.

Read a whole bare name, protecting internal keywords and retaining directives. wardley.md#keyword-and-name-boundaries: An id-name starts with an ASCII letter, digit or underscore, continues with those characters or hyphens and ends with a word character. Earlier rules still win: integer takes the 9 of 9a, whereas _a is a name. Non-ASCII bare names reject. Quoting a name avoids these keyword and bare-name restrictions. wardley.md#keyword-and-name-boundaries: A spaced-name starts with an ASCII letter. Continue with ASCII letters, digits, underscore, parentheses, ampersand, or a hyphen not immediately followed by >. Then repeat a nonempty space/tab run and another part starting with an ASCII letter or opening parenthesis, followed by the same continuation characters. Take as much as this form allows. Internal space/tab is authored name text; trailing padding is outside the name. A space followed by ampersand cannot start another part. wardley.md#common-boundaries-in-authored-components: A spaced-name is a text unit and can contain shared removals. common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary: A directive is trivia and not diagram text.
